slope/line: A straight line climbs at the same rate everywhere. Two x plus one rises two for every step of one, so its slope is two.
slope/shift: The plus one only sets the height. Two x minus two sits lower, but it tilts the same way: slope two. The constant never changes the slope.
slope/fall: A line that falls has a negative slope. Minus three x plus four drops three for every step: slope minus three.
slope/forms: However the line is written, find the number multiplying x. Three times, x minus one, is three x minus three: slope three. Half of two x plus four is x plus two: slope one.
slope/curve: A curve is steeper in some places than others. Take f of x equals x squared. How steep is it at x equals one?
slope/two: Pick a second point a step h to the right, at x equals two. Between them, f goes from one to four.
slope/rise: The rise is the later value minus the earlier one: four minus one, three. Over a run of one, the slope between the two points is three.
slope/formula: Written out: the slope between x and x plus h is f of x plus h, minus f of x, all over h.
shrink/shrink: Now shrink the step. With h equal to a half, the slope is two point five. With a tenth, it is two point one.
shrink/limit: As h shrinks toward zero, the slope settles on two. That limit is the derivative: f prime of one equals two.
shrink/tangent: The line with that slope just grazes the curve at x equals one. It is the tangent.
shrink/line: A straight line has nothing to shrink: every step gives the same slope. So the derivative of two x plus one is two, at every x.
nudge/rate: Read the derivative as a rate. Near x equals one, f changes about two times as much as x does.
nudge/right: Nudge x from one to one point zero one. f changes by about two times zero point zero one: zero point zero two.
nudge/value: So f of one point zero one is about one plus zero point zero two: one point zero two. The true value, one point zero two zero one, is very close.
nudge/left: Nudge to the left instead, to zero point nine nine, and the change flips sign: about minus zero point zero two, so f is near zero point nine eight.
nudge/rule: The same holds for any slope: the change in f is about f prime times the change in x.
sign/slide: The derivative changes from point to point. Slide the tangent along the curve.
sign/neg: On the left, f falls as x grows, and the slope is negative: minus three, at minus one point five.
sign/zero: At the bottom the tangent is level, and the slope is zero.
sign/pos: On the right, f rises, and the slope is positive: three.
sign/height: The sign is about direction, not height. At minus one point five, f is two point two five, well above zero, and still falling.
sign/table: Nearby values show the sign too. Around one, f goes zero point eight one, one, one point two one: rising, so the slope there is positive.
sign/dip: Around zero, f goes down to zero and back up. That is the bottom of a dip, where the slope is zero.
